facts.claim: Air Astana's first Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, registered EI-KZA, is undergoing flight testing at Boeing's Charleston facility and completed its first test flight on 1 October 2026.
The aircraft is the first of three 787-9s expected to enter commercial service during 2027, replacing the ageing Boeing 767-300ER fleet.
Delivery was originally expected in September 2026 but manufacturing delays pushed the handover to December, confirmed by Vice Minister of Transport Talgat Lastayev on 20 October.
The second Dreamliner is due in January 2027 and the third in August 2027, with about 20 regional sectors over two months for crew familiarisation before longer-haul service.
The airline aims to introduce US flights during the second half of 2027, subject to deliveries and operational approvals, and is assessing polar routings and payload requirements.

The November 2025 agreement for up to 15 additional 787-9s was finalised in February 2026 with five firm aircraft, five options and five purchase rights, potentially bringing the fleet to 18 Dreamliners with deliveries in 2032-2035 at about $7 billion including engines.

zh.title: 哈薩克阿斯塔納航空首架787-9夢幻客機展開試飛：拚2027年投入營運
zh.summary: 阿斯塔納航空首架波音787-9夢幻客機、機身編號EI-KZA，已於10月1日在波音查爾斯頓廠區完成首次試飛。首批3架預計2027年投入商業營運，逐步取代老舊的767-300ER機隊，並為開通美國直飛航線鋪路。
body: 阿斯塔納航空首架波音787-9夢幻客機已展開飛行測試，為哈薩克籍航空公司引進全新長程機隊、開通北美直飛航線邁出一步。該機機身編號EI-KZA，10月1日在波音南卡羅來納州查爾斯頓製造廠區完成首次試飛；航空公司在社群平台分享了原廠試飛計畫的照片，波音則正在完成必要的認證與交付程序。

航空公司預計首批3架787-9於2027年投入商業營運，取代老舊的767-300ER機隊並擴大國際航網。首架機原定2026年9月交付，但製造延誤使交機時程推遲至12月，哈薩克交通部副部長Talgat Lastayev於10月20日證實了修正後的時程。執行長Ibrahim Canliel表示，第二架將於2027年1月抵達、第三架於同年8月抵達；新機將先執行約20個區域航段、為期約2個月，讓機組熟悉新機型，再投入長程營運。

美國直飛航線是長程擴張的優先項目。Canliel表示，航空公司仍以2027年下半年開通美國航班為目標，但時程取決於飛機交付與營運許可；航空公司正在評估極地航路與載重需求，以確認能否不經停加油直飛。2025年11月，航空公司宣布與波音達成最多增購15架787-9的協議，協議於2026年2月敲定，包括5架確認訂單、5架選擇權與5架優先購買權；加上先前承諾，機隊最終可達18架，增購機預計2032年至2035年交付，含發動機在內的總價按製造商牌價約70億美元。787-9最大公布航程8300海里，遠高於767-300ER約6000海里的航程。

en.title: Air Astana's first Boeing 787-9 begins flight testing ahead of 2027 debut
en.summary: Air Astana's first Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, registered EI-KZA, completed its first test flight on October 1 at Boeing's Charleston facility, bringing the Kazakh carrier closer to launching long-haul services in 2027.
body: Air Astana's first Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner has begun flight testing, bringing the Kazakh carrier closer to introducing a new long-haul fleet and launching nonstop services to North America. The aircraft, registered EI-KZA, completed its first test flight on 1 October 2026 at Boeing's Charleston manufacturing facility in South Carolina. In an announcement posted on LinkedIn, Air Astana shared images from its factory flight-testing programme as Boeing completes the necessary certification and delivery procedures.

The airline expects its first three 787-9s to enter commercial service during 2027. The aircraft will replace its ageing Boeing 767-300ER fleet and support plans to expand its international network. Air Astana had originally expected to receive its first Dreamliner in September 2026, but manufacturing delays have pushed the anticipated handover to December. Kazakhstan's Vice Minister of Transport, Talgat Lastayev, confirmed the revised delivery schedule on 20 October. Chief executive Ibrahim Canliel has outlined a delivery schedule that would see the second Dreamliner arrive in January 2027 and the third in August 2027, with the aircraft initially operating about 20 regional sectors over two months to familiarise crews with the new type before entering longer-haul service.

Nonstop services to the US are a priority for the airline's long-haul expansion. Canliel said the carrier remains on course to introduce US flights during the second half of 2027, although the schedule depends on aircraft deliveries and operational approvals, and the airline is assessing polar routings and aircraft payload requirements to determine how it can operate the proposed services without intermediate fuel stops. In November 2025, the airline announced an agreement with Boeing for up to 15 additional 787-9s; the order was finalised in February 2026 and includes five firm aircraft, five options and five purchase rights. Combined with earlier commitments, Air Astana could ultimately operate a fleet of 18 Dreamliners, with deliveries under the additional order planned between 2032 and 2035 and a combined value, including engines, of approximately $7 billion based on manufacturer list prices. The 787-9 has a maximum published range of 8,300 nautical miles, compared with about 6,000 nautical miles for the 767-300ER.
